articles.headline: Belgium, India boost ties; pacts on defence manufacturing inked
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Belgian PM Bart De Wever held talks to bolster cooperation in defense, technology, and trade. The nations signed pacts for defense manufacturing and set a goal to double bilateral trade in five years. Discussions also covered resilient supply chains and collaboration in semiconductors, chemicals, and pharmaceuticals.

articles.headline: 100% chance of El Nino lasting till Feb '27: WMO
articles.summary: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) warned that El Nino conditions are likely to persist through February 2027 with nearly 100% probability. This could lead to record-breaking heat, extreme weather, and reduced rains for crops in several global regions. Scientists highlighted the phenomenon as 'unequivocal' and a sign of rapid warming.

articles.headline: Iran targets U.S. base in Kuwait as it mourns victims
articles.summary: Iran launched missiles and drones at a U.S. base in Kuwait following an airstrike on a wedding party in Iran that killed several civilians. Tehran described the move as a retaliatory strike. The U.S. military stated it was aware of the reports but maintained that it 'never targets civilians.' Tension in the region has escalated significantly.

articles.headline: Nvidia to buy Hugging Face for $13 billion
articles.summary: Chipmaker Nvidia has agreed to acquire the open-source AI platform Hugging Face in a deal valued at $13 billion. The acquisition includes up to $1 billion in equity-based retention programs for employees. The move is seen as a strategic effort by Nvidia to strengthen its software ecosystem as major tech firms build their own AI chips.

articles.headline: 31-member JPC set up to examine FCRA bill
articles.summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has constituted a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) to review the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. The committee, chaired by BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal, includes members from the Congress, TMC, and other parties. The panel is expected to submit its report in the next parliament session.

articles.headline: Missing numbers spike at hydroproject sites in Nepal
articles.summary: The count of missing persons in flood-hit areas of Nepal has risen to 966, primarily at four major hydroelectric project sites following a glacial outburst. Rescue teams from four nations have joined efforts to reach workers trapped in tunnels. The concentration of missing persons is highest at the Upper Trishuli-1 and Rasuwagadhi project sites.

articles.headline: Estonia minister exits over deal for shells with India-linked firm
articles.summary: Estonia's defense minister Hanno Pevkur resigned after controversy erupted over a botched artillery shell deal for Ukraine involving an Indian-owned company, Dataset SRL. The deal faced delivery issues and allegations of wrongdoing. Pevkur stated he decided to resign to avoid further political damage to the government.

articles.headline: Capital's garbage crisis piles up amid contract tangle
articles.summary: Delhi faces a growing garbage crisis as landfills overflow and legal disputes delay the transition to new long-term waste disposal contracts. Large parts of the city are struggling with unsanitary conditions as the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) seeks to overhaul its waste management infrastructure amid bureaucratic hurdles.

articles.headline: Delhi ex-minister Satyendar Jain gets bail in STP case
articles.summary: A Delhi court granted bail to former minister Satyendar Jain in a corruption case related to a Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) tender. The court observed that the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) failed to provide sufficient evidence to justify his continued detention. Jain had been in custody since May 2022 in a separate money laundering case.

articles.headline: IndiGo flight diverted after pilot faces medical issue
articles.summary: A Muscat-bound IndiGo flight from Bengaluru was diverted to Muscat after the pilot-in-command faced a medical emergency. The aircraft landed safely, and the pilot received immediate medical attention. Passengers were provided refreshments while the airline arranged for an alternative crew to complete the flight to its final destination.

articles.headline: Feminist icon Gloria Steinem passes away at 92
articles.summary: Gloria Steinem, the American writer and activist who became a global face of the women's liberation movement, has died at the age of 92. Known for co-founding Ms. Magazine and her work in civil rights, Steinem's legacy includes decades of advocacy for gender equality. Her foundation stated she died peacefully at her home in New York.

articles.headline: West Bengal schools ensure national song sung in full
articles.summary: Schools in West Bengal have started singing all six stanzas of 'Vande Mataram' following a state government directive. Education Minister Bratya Basu stated that the move aims to instill patriotic values. The government had previously warned schools of action if the national song was not performed in its entirety during morning assemblies.

articles.headline: Food safety officials inspect Blinkit facility in Mangaluru
articles.summary: Mangaluru food safety officials inspected a Blinkit warehouse after a customer reported finding a worm in an egg delivered by the platform. The facility was issued a notice and temporary closure for cleaning and sanitization. Officials collected samples for further testing and warned the service provider about maintaining hygiene standards.

articles.headline: Karnataka Assembly special session to discuss Kasturirangan report
articles.summary: The Karnataka government will convene a special legislative session to discuss the Kasturirangan report on Western Ghats and the severe drought situation in the state. The session aims to formulate a unified stand against the report's recommendations and plan relief measures for drought-hit districts. Farmers' organizations have welcomed the move.

articles.headline: Karnataka approves ₹25 crore for fodder in drought areas
articles.summary: The Karnataka cabinet has approved an allocation of ₹25 crore to provide fodder for livestock in 135 drought-affected taluks. The government plans to set up fodder banks and provide subsidies to farmers to prevent distress sale of cattle. This is part of a larger ₹600 crore relief package being planned for agriculture and rural sectors.

articles.headline: Telangana minister Konda Surekha sacked over daughter's remarks
articles.summary: Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy has dropped Konda Surekha from the state cabinet after her daughter made controversial remarks about senior political leaders. The decision followed a directive from the Congress high command. Surekha, who held the endowments and forest portfolios, expressed shock but stated she would remain loyal to the party.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu plans new secretariat and Olympic City
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay announced the construction of a new administrative secretariat complex and a 'Sports Olympic City' in Chennai. The projects, estimated to cost over ₹1,200 crore, aim to modernize state administration and provide world-class facilities for athletes. The CM stated that the secretariat would be a symbol of Tamil culture and efficiency.

articles.headline: Andhra ACB arrests TTD deputy executive officer
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested a Deputy Executive Officer of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) for allegedly possessing assets disproportionate to his known sources of income. Raids at multiple locations in Tirupati and Nellore led to the seizure of cash, gold, and property documents valued at several crores.

articles.headline: Rajnath Singh unveils 10-year roadmap for defence diplomacy
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh launched 'Raksha', a 10-year roadmap to strengthen India's defense ties and bolster exports. The strategy focuses on proactive global cooperation, technology transfer, and joint manufacturing with friendly nations. India aims to reach ₹50,000 crore in annual defense exports by 2030 through this initiative.

articles.headline: Mayawati removes nephew Akash Anand from BSP post
articles.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati has removed her nephew Akash Anand from the post of national coordinator. She stated that Anand needs 'more maturity' before taking on such a senior role. This is the second time he has been removed from the position, reflecting internal shifts within the BSP leadership ahead of upcoming regional polls.

articles.headline: Abhishek Banerjee's Kolkata office ransacked and looted
articles.summary: A group of armed, masked individuals allegedly ransacked and looted the office of TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee in South Kolkata. The intruders reportedly stole computers and sensitive documents. The TMC has alleged a political conspiracy, while the Kolkata police have launched a high-level probe and detained several suspects for questioning.

articles.headline: 306 killed in Manipur ethnic violence since 2023
articles.summary: Manipur Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam informed the state assembly that at least 306 people have been killed in ethnic violence since May 2023. He added that 49 people remain missing. The government is working with the Centre to restore peace and provide relief to thousands of displaced families currently living in temporary camps.

articles.headline: Centre invites Ladakh leaders for talks on Sept 9
articles.summary: The Union Home Ministry has invited leaders from the Leh Apex Body and Kargil Democratic Alliance for a new round of talks in Delhi on September 9. The discussion will focus on demands for statehood, constitutional safeguards under the Sixth Schedule, and job reservations for locals. Previous rounds of talks had ended in a deadlock.

articles.headline: Accused stabs sexual assault survivor to death in Haryana
articles.summary: A 24-year-old woman, who was a survivor of sexual assault, was allegedly stabbed to death by the accused in Haryana's Jind district. The incident occurred while the accused was out on bail. The victim's family has alleged police negligence in providing security. The police have registered a fresh case of murder and are conducting raids to nab the accused.

articles.headline: UP rains: 5 dead as Ganga crosses danger mark
articles.summary: Heavy monsoon rains in Uttar Pradesh have resulted in five deaths and caused the Ganga to flow above the danger mark in several districts. Flooding has affected low-lying areas in Varanasi and Prayagraj. CM Yogi Adityanath has directed district officials to expedite relief operations and evacuate people from vulnerable riverside settlements.

articles.headline: India seeks tariff advantage in bilateral US trade deal
articles.summary: The Indian government is pushing for preferential tariff treatment in its ongoing trade negotiations with the United States. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India seeks 'comparative advantage' to boost exports of labor-intensive goods. Finalizing the deal could significantly increase bilateral trade and provide a stable framework for investments.

articles.headline: Services sector growth slows to four-year low in August
articles.summary: India's services sector growth decelerated to its slowest pace in four years in August, according to the HSBC India Services PMI. The index dropped to 53.3 from 54.3 in July. While still in expansion territory, the slowdown was attributed to weaker demand and competitive pressures, marking the softest growth since March 2022.

articles.headline: BCCI backs Rohit Sharma; notes schedule impact on team
articles.summary: The BCCI has officially backed Rohit Sharma to continue as captain despite a recent slump in India's ODI performance. In a review meeting, the board noted that 'too much cricket' and a congested schedule are impacting player fitness and performance. The BCCI plans to implement better workload management ahead of the next World Cup cycle.

articles.headline: Yashvir Singh replaces injured Neeraj Chopra for Asian Games
articles.summary: Javelin thrower Yashvir Singh has been named as a replacement for Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra in the Indian squad for the Asian Games. Chopra was forced to withdraw due to a persistent groin injury. Yashvir, a bronze medalist at the Commonwealth Games, is expected to lead India's challenge in the event alongside Kishore Jena.

articles.headline: Handwriting on tissue paper triggers probe into Air India Express crew
articles.summary: Security agencies and police are investigating cabin crew members of an Air India Express flight after a tissue paper with a handwritten bomb threat was found in the lavatory. All 40 people on board, including crew, have undergone handwriting sampling. The aircraft was diverted to Ahmedabad following the discovery of the note during the Dammam-Delhi flight.

articles.headline: India and Belgium to double bilateral trade via defense and energy
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Belgian Prime Minister Alexander De Croo agreed to double bilateral trade within five years, focusing on defense, green energy, and semiconductors. The leaders signed ten agreements, including the joint manufacturing of defense equipment and cooperation on clean technology and maritime security during talks in New Delhi.

articles.headline: Govt to permit emission retrofit kits in heavy commercial vehicles
articles.summary: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari announced that the government will allow the installation of retrofit emission-control devices in older heavy vehicles to reduce pollution. The move aims to cut particulate matter emissions by up to 90%. Technology developed by an IIT Delhi startup will enable BS-IV and BS-III trucks to comply with BS-VI standards at a cost of ₹4,000-₹5,000.

articles.headline: Kenya orders Tata Chemicals to cease operations in Kajiado
articles.summary: Kenya's President William Ruto has ordered Tata Chemicals Magadi Ltd to stop operations in Kajiado County, claiming the local community has not benefited from the company's presence. Ruto criticized the century-old contract for mineral extraction and asked the company to vacate the area. Tata Chemicals has operated the Magadi resource since acquiring it in 2005.

articles.headline: Ladakh's seven districts to get autonomous hill councils for self-governance
articles.summary: The Union government announced that all seven districts of the Union Territory of Ladakh will now have autonomous hill councils. The move is intended to provide local self-governance and empower the region's inhabitants. Council elections will be held soon to establish administrative bodies similar to those already existing in Leh and Kargil.

articles.headline: Bengaluru bikers demand refund of road tax amid flyover restrictions
articles.summary: Two-wheeler riders in Bengaluru are demanding a refund of life-time road tax following restrictions on their access to major flyovers, including the Electronics City and KIA elevated roads. Bikers staged a 'Last Ride' protest, arguing that they paid substantial taxes for infrastructure that is now being denied to them based on safety concerns cited by police.

articles.headline: Aero India 2027 to be held in Yelahanka from February 8
articles.summary: The 16th edition of Aero India will take place at the Air Force Station, Yelahanka, from February 8 to 12, 2027. The Ministry of Defence confirmed the dates for the biennial air show and aviation exhibition, which serves as a major platform for global aerospace and defense firms to showcase technology and sign strategic agreements.

articles.headline: Bone marrow transplants provide second chance for children with PKD
articles.summary: Pediatric patients suffering from Polycystic Kidney Disease (PKD) and associated bone marrow failure are finding new life through transplants in Bengaluru. Doctors highlight successful cases where children received marrow from half-matched parents or unrelated donors, overcoming severe anemia and frequent infection risks associated with the genetic condition.

articles.headline: Karnataka to establish dedicated department for NRI and overseas affairs
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has approved the creation of a Department of Global Investment and Overseas Affairs to support NRIs and attract foreign investment. The single-window system will handle welfare issues for non-resident Kannadigas and facilitate business ventures. The cabinet also approved a 3-day special legislative session from Sept 21 to discuss drought and farmers' issues.

articles.headline: Ballari Chalo rally: BJP seeks revival against Karnataka government
articles.summary: The BJP's ongoing 10-day 'Ballari Chalo' padayatra from Raichur is being viewed as a crucial attempt to regain political momentum in Karnataka. Led by state president B.Y. Vijayendra, the march targets the Congress government over alleged scams and lack of development. The rally aims to consolidate the party's base ahead of upcoming local body and assembly elections.

articles.headline: Karnataka High Court seeks technical report on Hebbal Lake tunnel
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court has requested a technical presentation from an engineering expert regarding the proposed Hebbal Lake tunnel project. The court is investigating whether the construction of the short tunnel will adversely impact the lake's water levels or inflow and outflow. Petitioners have raised concerns about the environmental integrity of the water body.

articles.headline: Incorrect India boundary on Anthropic website leads to government notice
articles.summary: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has issued a notice to AI company Anthropic after its website allegedly displayed an incorrect map of India. The map depicted parts of Arunachal Pradesh and Ladakh with dotted lines, prompting a complaint from a presentation attendee. The government emphasized that accurate mapping is a legal requirement for digital platforms.

articles.headline: Belgium condemns Pahalgam terror attack in solidarity with India
articles.summary: During bilateral talks in New Delhi, Belgium condemned the recent terror attack in Pahalgam and expressed solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism. Both nations agreed to enhance intelligence sharing and cooperation on counter-terrorism. The leaders also discussed clean energy, reliable supply chains, and a new mobility agreement for students and professionals.

articles.headline: VHP's restrictive rules for Durga Puja face pushback in Bengal
articles.summary: The Vishwa Hindu Parishad's (VHP) set of 'dos and don'ts' for Durga Puja, which includes banning non-Hindus from organizing committees and prohibiting non-vegetarian food near pandals, has met with resistance in West Bengal. Puja organizers and residents in Kolkata argue that the festival is a cultural event that transcends religious boundaries and should remain inclusive.

articles.headline: Sudden resignation of popular IAS officer Divya Mittal sparks speculation
articles.summary: The unexplained resignation of IAS officer Divya Mittal, who gained popularity for her accessibility and hands-on administration in Uttar Pradesh districts like Mirzapur, has left colleagues and admirers wondering about her next move. Mittal, a 2013-batch officer and IIT-IIM alumna, cited a 'debt to this soil' in her farewell but has not disclosed her future plans or reasons for leaving.

articles.headline: Apple’s pivot to Indian manufacturing shows smart ecosystem integration
articles.summary: Apple is deepening its manufacturing presence in India by integrating with the country's open digital infrastructure, including UPI and ONDC. Reports indicate the tech giant is moving beyond assembly to component manufacturing, aiming to make India a critical hub in its global supply chain. The strategy fits India's PLI schemes and goal of becoming a smartphone export powerhouse.

articles.headline: Rajnath Singh urges Belgium to restrict sensitive tech sharing with Pakistan
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh expressed India's concern regarding the potential transfer of sensitive military technology from Belgium to Pakistan. During talks with Belgian Defence Minister Ludivine Dedonder, Singh emphasized the need for responsible export controls. The two nations discussed deeper industrial cooperation, including the co-production of aerospace and maritime products.

articles.headline: SC: Poverty and migration contribute to child delinquency
articles.summary: The Supreme Court observed that poverty, illiteracy, and the discriminatory environment resulting from rural-to-urban migration are major factors driving children toward delinquency. The court emphasized that the state must address socio-economic roots rather than just focusing on punitive measures for juvenile offenders, particularly those from marginalized backgrounds.

articles.headline: West Bengal CM to establish 1,000 Vidya Bharati schools annually
articles.summary: Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee announced a plan to set up 1,000 new schools annually under the 'Vidya Bharati' initiative to improve the quality of education across the state. The program will prioritize districts like Murshidabad and South 24 Parganas. The move aims to provide modern facilities and a standardized curriculum to bridge the educational gap in rural areas.

articles.headline: Karnataka government withdraws controversial park bill following public pressure
articles.summary: Following widespread protests, the Karnataka government has withdrawn the proposed park bill that would have allowed commercial activities and construction within public parks. Deputy CM D.K. Shivakumar stated the decision was made to address citizen concerns and ensure the protection of the city's green spaces. The bill will be re-evaluated for future modifications.

articles.headline: ISRO shuffles leadership at key centers following superannuations
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has undergone a major leadership reshuffle at several key centers, including the UR Rao Satellite Centre (URSC) and the Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC). The changes were triggered by the retirement of senior officials and aim to bring new focus to upcoming missions like Gaganyaan. Dr. D.K. Singh has been moved to lead URSC.

articles.headline: EAM Jaishankar: Diplomacy, not oil, is key to peace in Ukraine
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated that ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict depends on sincere diplomacy rather than narratives about oil trade. Speaking after a meeting with President Zelenskyy's team, Jaishankar reiterated India's stance that the world expects an early end to the war and that India is willing to contribute to any credible peace process through dialogue.

articles.headline: US warns of sanctions over Modi’s meeting with Iranian President
articles.summary: The US government has cautioned that any trade or cooperation agreements following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian could be subject to sanctions. Washington emphasized its firm stance on isolating Iran's nuclear and regional activities, while New Delhi maintains its strategic autonomy in pursuing regional connectivity through Iran.

articles.headline: Nepal flood: Vehicle plugs tunnel mouth, saving 40 trapped workers
articles.summary: In a miraculous escape, 40 workers at a hydropower project in Nepal were saved when a flood-swept vehicle plugged the entrance of the tunnel they were trapped in. The vehicle acted as an accidental barrier against a massive flow of mud and debris. Rescuers worked for over 30 hours to safely evacuate the workers, who had lost all communication with the outside world.

articles.headline: US government supports OpenAI in copyright lawsuit by New York Times
articles.summary: The US Justice Department has filed a court document supporting OpenAI in its ongoing copyright lawsuit against The New York Times. The government argues that fair use protections should apply to the training of AI models using publicly available text. The brief suggests that overly restrictive copyright laws could hinder the development of transformative AI technologies.

articles.headline: India's 7.8% GDP growth is remarkable despite global headwinds: FM
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that India's 7.8% GDP growth in the last quarter is a testament to the country's economic resilience amid global disruptions. She highlighted that India continues to be the fastest-growing major economy. The growth was driven by robust performance in manufacturing and services, supported by government infrastructure spending.

articles.headline: Sebi to revise CAS settlement method for derivative trades
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is set to revise the settlement price mechanism for derivatives following a consultation period. The new method for Closing Auction Session (CAS) seeks to reduce market volatility and prevent price manipulation. Sebi has proposed a system that better reflects true volume-weighted average prices during the final trading hour.

articles.headline: Nvidia’s price hike may increase costs for Indian AI infrastructure
articles.summary: Nvidia's plan to raise prices for its high-end AI chips by up to 15% is expected to significantly increase infrastructure costs for Indian startups and cloud providers. Industry experts warn that the hike will lead to higher deployment costs for AI models and data centers. Firms are now re-evaluating their expansion plans and looking for more power-efficient alternative hardware.

articles.headline: Dry lakebeds in Karnataka transformed into 95MW solar fields
articles.summary: Karnataka's energy department has successfully converted several dry lakebeds in rural Bengaluru into solar power plants, generating 95MW of electricity daily. The initiative uses solar pumps to provide irrigation to nearby farms while feeding surplus power into the state grid. The project has been hailed as a model for utilizing unusable land for sustainable energy production.

articles.headline: CBI to probe Disha Salian case following High Court orders
articles.summary: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has taken over the probe into the death of Disha Salian, former manager of actor Sushant Singh Rajput, following directions from the Bombay High Court. The court noted lapses in the initial police investigation and emphasized the need for a thorough inquiry to address inconsistencies in reports regarding her death in June 2020.

articles.headline: Office-to-home trend drives premium housing demand in Bengaluru
articles.summary: The expansion of Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in Bengaluru is creating a ripple effect on the city's real estate, driving demand for premium homes near office corridors. Residential prices in areas like Whitefield and Sarjapur Road have appreciated significantly as employees prefer living close to their workplaces to avoid traffic congestion.

articles.headline: Centre Sees No Cost Pain for RBI on Dollar Deluge
articles.summary: The RBI is expected to manage a $127-billion inflow from maturing FCNR(B) deposits and swap facilities without high sterilisation costs. Treasury gains and existing liquidity tools are projected to offset potential hedging expenses of approximately ₹36,000 crore. Analysts believe the central bank's healthy contingency buffer will allow it to absorb the excess liquidity smoothly.

articles.headline: Green Flag Up for Purvah to Buy Welspun RE Arm
articles.summary: Purvah Green Power is set to acquire Welspun New Energy for an enterprise value of approximately ₹2,500 crore. The deal will add 45 MW of operational projects and a 5 GW pipeline to Purvah's portfolio. The acquisition aligns with the company's goal to build a 10 GW green power capacity through both organic growth and acquisitions by 2030.

articles.headline: Jio Sets Eyes on Navratri-Diwali Period to Launch Mega $4b IPO
articles.summary: Reliance Industries' telecom arm, Jio Platforms, is planning to launch its $4-billion initial public offering (IPO) during the festive window of Navratri to Diwali. The company is currently finalising international and domestic roadshows. The IPO is expected to be one of India's largest, potentially valuing the company significantly higher than previous funding rounds.

articles.headline: Indian Cos Rush to Align with UAE Minimum Tax
articles.summary: Multinational companies operating in the UAE are restructuring their operations to comply with a new 15% minimum tax regime starting January 2025. The tax applies to groups with consolidated global revenues exceeding €750 million. The move aims to align with OECD Pillar 2 global tax standards and may impact free zone entities previously enjoying tax-exempt status.

articles.headline: Indian Co in Middle of Ukrainian Arms Supply Scandal
articles.summary: An Indian firm, Power Trans, is under investigation for its alleged role in an arms supply chain that diverted artillery ammunition meant for Estonia to Ukraine. The Estonian Ministry of Defence has initiated legal proceedings, claiming breach of contract. The Indian firm denies allegations of unauthorized diversion and maintains the equipment met specified quality standards.

articles.headline: India and Belgium to Expand Defence, Trade Partnerships
articles.summary: India and Belgium have agreed to deepen ties in defense manufacturing and trade, following a meeting between PM Modi and Belgian counterpart Alexander De Croo. The collaboration includes technology transfer for small arms and potential joint ventures in critical minerals. Both nations reaffirmed their commitment to combatting cross-border terrorism and strengthening maritime security.

articles.headline: FDA Nod Must in Maha for Iftaars, Langars, Weddings
articles.summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration has mandated prior permission for large-scale food distribution at religious and social events. Organizers of iftaars, bhandaras, and weddings must now file a proforma detailing the caterer and ingredients used. The move aims to prevent incidents of mass food poisoning and ensure adherence to safety standards during peak festive seasons.

articles.headline: Sugar Cosmetics Value May Melt 80% in ₹150cr Bailout
articles.summary: D2C beauty brand Sugar Cosmetics is in talks to raise ₹140-150 crore from existing investor A91 Partners at a valuation of ₹500-600 crore. This represents a steep 80% drop from its previous peak valuation of ₹3,000 crore. The firm is struggling with mounting losses and intense competition in the beauty segment, necessitating fresh capital to sustain operations.

articles.headline: CAS Case: Sebi to Review F&O Settlement Pricing
articles.summary: SEBI is reviewing the methodology for determining settlement prices for derivative contracts following market feedback. The move follows concerns over sharp price swings during the recent rollout of the new calling auction session (CAS) in the equity cash segment. A consultation paper on the proposed changes is expected to be released within a week.

articles.headline: Large Cos Feel Margin Heat More than Smaller Peers
articles.summary: An analysis of 3,340 companies shows that large-cap firms have experienced a sharper contraction in operating margins compared to mid and small-cap peers. Large-cap margins fell by 230 basis points year-on-year to 13.5% in the June quarter. Input cost pressures and a higher base effect are cited as primary reasons for the relative underperformance of bigger corporate entities.

articles.headline: Labels are Now Main Course for Top F&B Chiefs
articles.summary: Top food and beverage executives are intensifying their focus on label compliance and ingredient safety following recent regulatory crackdowns. Companies are diverting funds from marketing to strengthen internal audits and third-party testing. FSSAI has issued over 150 notices to brands for misleading claims, forcing boards to prioritize product transparency over brand image.

articles.headline: Electronics Cos Plug into Cheaper Inputs, Localisation
articles.summary: Indian electronics manufacturers are shifting from copper to aluminum and increasing domestic sourcing to mitigate rising raw material costs. Copper prices have risen nearly 18% year-on-year, prompting companies like Voltas and Bajaj Electricals to redesign products. Localisation efforts have increased from 15% to nearly 40% in some segments to stabilize consumer pricing.

articles.headline: Bring Two GDP Series, with Old & New Base: Sen
articles.summary: Former chief statistician Pronab Sen has suggested that the government should release two separate GDP series with both the old and new base years for at least five years. This dual reporting would help identify if 'double deflation' is correctly capturing real economic growth. India last updated its GDP base year to 2011-12 and has delayed further revisions due to data inconsistencies.

articles.headline: Services Activity Grows in Aug, But Near 4-Year Low
articles.summary: India's services sector expanded in August driven by strong domestic demand, but the pace of growth hit a near four-year low. The HSBC Services Business Activity Index fell to 54.1 from 55.3 in July. While business confidence remains high, rising input costs and a slight moderation in new orders have slowed the momentum compared to the rapid expansion seen earlier this year.

articles.headline: AB Group Forays into Wires and Cables Business
articles.summary: Aditya Birla Group has announced its entry into the ₹1.8 lakh crore wires and cables market under the brand 'Ultravolt'. The new venture, housed under UltraTech Cement, plans to invest ₹1,800 crore to become a top five player within five years. The company will leverage its massive dealer network of over 1 lakh retailers to challenge established players like Polycab and Havells.

articles.headline: AI Outage: Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok Services Hit
articles.summary: Major AI platforms including OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude experienced significant service disruptions on Thursday. Users reported errors in generating responses and interface failures worldwide. The outages were attributed to technical issues at infrastructure providers like AWS and internal server errors, highlighting the fragility of global AI dependencies.

articles.headline: FSSAI Mulls Ban on Non-dairy Paneer
articles.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is considering a ban on 'analog paneer,' which uses vegetable oils instead of milk fats. The regulator noted that such products are often sold as genuine dairy paneer, misleading consumers. New rules may restrict the use of the term 'paneer' for non-dairy alternatives and mandate clear labeling to distinguish plant-based substitutes.

articles.headline: Wipro Kawasaki to Invest ₹1,000cr for Hydraulic Pump Plant
articles.summary: Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery plans to invest ₹1,000 crore to set up a new manufacturing unit for hydraulic pumps at Harohalli, Karnataka. The plant, sprawling over 30 acres, is expected to create 1,200 jobs and produce over 2 lakh hydraulic pumps annually. The facility will cater to the growing demand in the construction and earthmoving equipment sectors.

articles.headline: Clock is Ticking as Missing No. Tops 5,000 in Nepal
articles.summary: The death toll from catastrophic flash floods in Nepal has risen to 1,259, with over 5,083 people still reported missing. International aid is pouring in as rescue operations face challenges from destroyed infrastructure and blocked mountain passes. The Nepal government has requested satellite imagery and specialist rescue teams to help locate survivors in the remote Langtang region.

articles.headline: States Draw Up Action Plan For Pollution Season
articles.summary: NCR states including Punjab, Haryana, and UP have submitted a 7-point action plan to the Centre to combat stubble burning and winter pollution. Measures include increased subsidies for biomass machinery and strict monitoring of thermal plants. The plan also includes dust control protocols for construction sites and emergency traffic restrictions if AQI levels cross critical thresholds.

articles.headline: Warring Row Tests Cong's Dalit Pitch
articles.summary: Internal friction in the Punjab Congress has intensified as state unit chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring faces scrutiny over alleged anti-Dalit remarks. The row has sparked protests from within the party's Scheduled Caste wing, potentially undermining the Congress party's efforts to woo the Dalit vote bank ahead of upcoming state elections. Central leadership has called for a detailed report.

articles.headline: Recruitment Scam: K'taka Suspends IAS Officer Gangwar
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has suspended senior IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar following his arrest by the CID in a recruitment scam. The investigation involves alleged irregularities in the recruitment of gazetted probationers by the KPSC. Gangwar is accused of abusing his position to facilitate illegal selections, and a special court has remanded him to judicial custody for 14 days.

articles.headline: The Un-Unicorn Slice Bags $100m at Slashed $470m Value
articles.summary: Fintech startup Slice has raised $100 million in fresh funding but at a valuation of $470 million, a 64% drop from its previous peak of $1.3 billion. The round was led by Tarsadia Investments and GGV Capital. The funding comes as the company pivots to a full-service banking model following regulatory changes in the prepaid card segment that impacted its primary business model.

articles.headline: India's Semicon Dream Needs Time to Bloom: Sima AI
articles.summary: Sima AI CEO Krishna Rangasayee stated that India's ambition to become a global semiconductor hub will require decades to fully mature. While government incentives are a good start, he emphasized the need for a robust talent pool and indigenous manufacturing ecosystems. He warned that high upfront costs and long gestation periods are major challenges for domestic startups in this space.

articles.headline: Apple Facing $2.7b UK Lawsuit over App Tracking Rules
articles.summary: Apple is facing a $2.7-billion class-action lawsuit in the UK, alleging that it used its dominant market position to impose unfair app tracking rules. The claim argues that Apple's 'App Tracking Transparency' framework harmed third-party developers while giving its own advertising services an unfair advantage. Apple has denied the allegations, stating the feature was designed for user privacy.

articles.headline: SC Approves Settlement; NSE's Mega IPO Plans Clear Hurdle
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has approved a settlement between SEBI and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) regarding the long-standing co-location case. The settlement clears a major regulatory hurdle for the NSE's proposed ₹31,000-crore initial public offering. The exchange had been barred from accessing the capital markets for years due to allegations of giving certain brokers preferential access.

articles.headline: Alcaraz Wants to Break Free
articles.summary: Tennis star Carlos Alcaraz advanced to the third round of the US Open with a straight-sets victory. Despite his dominant performance, the Spaniard expressed concerns over the grueling ATP calendar and its physical toll on players. He called for a review of the schedule to prevent long-term injuries, noting that he felt physically drained following the recent Olympic Games in Paris.

articles.headline: Drive on Road to Viksit Bharat: PM to Auto Cos
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi exhorted the Indian automobile industry to lead the transition toward green and sustainable mobility. Speaking at the SIAM annual convention, he urged manufacturers to increase R&D investment and focus on global exports. He emphasized that the auto sector's growth is central to India's vision of becoming a developed nation (Viksit Bharat) by 2047.

articles.headline: Preferential Tariffs with US Deal: Goyal
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India will seek preferential tariff advantages in its upcoming trade deal with the US, similar to those enjoyed by competing economies. The move aims to protect Indian farmers and small businesses while increasing market access for textiles and gems. Negotiations are focused on ensuring a balanced trade partnership without compromising domestic interests.

articles.headline: Sebi Plans Net Settlement for MF Trades in Cash Mkt
articles.summary: SEBI is considering a plan to allow net settlement for mutual fund transactions in the cash market to improve capital efficiency. Currently, these trades are settled on a gross basis, requiring higher liquidity. The proposed change would allow MFs to offset buy and sell obligations within the same settlement cycle, potentially lowering the costs for asset management companies and investors.

articles.headline: MS Pill Trial Success a Boost for Novartis' Drug Pipeline
articles.summary: Novartis announced that its experimental oral pill for Multiple Sclerosis (MS) has met its primary goals in a late-stage clinical trial. The drug showed significant efficacy in reducing brain lesions and relapse rates compared to existing treatments. Analysts expect the drug to become a blockbuster with peak sales potential exceeding $1.5 billion, strengthening Novartis' neurology portfolio.

articles.headline: Home Prices Rise Twice as Fast as Construction Costs
articles.summary: A report by Anarock Group indicates that residential property prices in India's top seven cities have risen twice as fast as construction costs over the last five years. While construction costs increased by 25-30%, average home prices surged by over 50%. The gap is attributed to high demand-supply mismatch and rising land acquisition costs in prime urban locations like Mumbai and Gurugram.

articles.headline: India Ready to Help End War, Says EAM in Kyiv
articles.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, during a historic visit to Kyiv, stated that India is prepared to contribute to any effort to end the Ukraine conflict. He emphasized that India supports a peaceful resolution through diplomacy and dialogue. The visit marks a significant shift in India's engagement with Ukraine, focusing on humanitarian aid and potential reconstruction support.

articles.headline: Smriti Mandhana steers India into semi-finals with record century
articles.summary: Indian batter Smriti Mandhana scored a record-breaking 124 off 64 balls to lead the Indian women's team into the semi-finals of the Asian Games cricket tournament. Her performance helped India secure a dominant 137-run victory over Hong Kong. Mandhana's century is the highest score by an Indian woman in T20 Internationals, surpassing her own previous records.

articles.headline: IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar suspended over recruitment scam
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar following allegations of his involvement in a recruitment scam at the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC). The Enforcement Directorate and CID are investigating claims of financial irregularities and shielding of accused persons during his tenure. Gangwar was previously serving as an IAS officer in Bengaluru.

articles.headline: State Withdraws Parks Bill After Citizens' Protests
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has decided to withdraw the controversial Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill following intense public protests. The bill sought to allow the government to take over up to 5% of park land for public utility purposes. Activists feared the move would lead to the commercialization of green spaces in Bengaluru and other urban centers.

articles.headline: Madras HC: Main Medium Must be Tamil; TN to Centre
articles.summary: The Madras High Court has passed a resolution stating that Tamil should be the primary medium of instruction in schools and the principal language of the judiciary in Tamil Nadu. The court urged the Union government to recognize Tamil's status as a classical language by ensuring its use in all central government offices in the state. The move is seen as a push for linguistic identity.

articles.headline: BCI has No Power to Take Action against Law Students: SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the Bar Council of India (BCI) lacks the statutory authority to take disciplinary action against law students for misconduct within universities. The court clarified that BCI's powers are limited to legal professionals enrolled as advocates. Universities retain the sole jurisdiction to penalize students for behavior occurring during their academic courses.

articles.headline: NHRC Seeks Reports on Insta CSAM Ads
articles.summary: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has issued notices to Meta and the Ministry of Electronics and IT regarding reports of advertisements on Instagram promoting child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The commission expressed grave concern over the automated algorithms that allowed such content to be monetized. It has sought a detailed report on safety measures within four weeks.
